Converts an explicit lifetime, type, inferred type, const, or inferred const HIR argument into a `ty::GenericArg`, including optional stability checks and special handling for `_` in type positions. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `allow_ty_infer`, `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, and `ct_infer`.

Synthesizes a missing generic argument by inferring lifetimes, inferring types, applying type defaults, or inferring/defaulting consts while guarding against prior type errors. This method explicitly calls `tcx`, `re_infer`, `ty_infer`, and `ct_infer`.

Separately converts associated type/const bindings and constraint clauses from HIR generic arguments into `ConvertedBinding` records for later predicate generation. This method explicitly calls `ast_ty_to_ty` and `tcx`.

Builds substitutions for an associated item path using already-known parent substitutions, while forbidding associated type bindings in this position. Calls `create_substs_for_ast_path` to compute the instantiated arguments, and if bindings are present calls `tcx` and `prohibit_assoc_ty_binding` to emit the diagnostic.

Creates a monomorphic trait reference from a parsed trait path and explicit `Self` type after first forbidding generics on all non-final path segments. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`.

Internal worker for poly trait-ref instantiation: it builds trait generic arguments, collects associated bindings, creates a bound `TraitRef`, pushes the trait bound into `Bounds`, and converts associated bindings into predicates while handling invalid negative-bound bindings. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path`, `tcx`, `create_assoc_bindings_for_generic_args`, and `add_predicates_for_ast_type_binding`.

Top-level entry point for instantiating a parsed trait bound into polymorphic bounds data: it extracts the final path segment, rejects generics on earlier segments, checks for internal `Fn`-trait diagnostics, and delegates the actual construction to `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics`, `complain_about_internal_fn_trait`, and `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`.

Instantiates a trait bound for a lang-item trait by resolving the lang item to a trait `DefId`, fabricating an invalid path segment placeholder, and delegating to `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`. This method explicitly calls `tcx` and `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`.

Builds a non-polymorphic `ty::TraitRef` from a trait path segment and `Self` type by first creating trait arguments and then rejecting associated type bindings in this context. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_trait_ref` and `tcx`.

Creates substitutions for a trait reference, supplying the trait `Self` type and reporting internal `Fn`-trait misuse first. Calls `complain_about_internal_fn_trait`, then delegates to `create_substs_for_ast_path`.

Checks whether the given trait defines an associated type with the specified name by querying the type context’s associated items and searching for a `ty::AssocKind::Type` entry. Calls `tcx`, `associated_items`, `find_by_name_and_kind`, and `is_some`.

Checks whether the given trait defines an associated const with the specified name by querying the type context’s associated items and searching for a `ty::AssocKind::Const` entry. Calls `tcx`, `associated_items`, `find_by_name_and_kind`, and `is_some`.

Adds the implicit `Sized` bound for a type parameter unless an explicit `?Sized` relaxation is present, and warns about unsupported relaxed default bounds like `?Trait`. Calls `tcx` to inspect lang items and emit diagnostics, scans where-clause bounds via `is_param_bound` and `to_def_id`, and finally calls `push_sized` when `Sized` should be added.

Converts a stream of HIR generic bounds into semantic bounds for a type parameter. For trait bounds it calls `instantiate_poly_trait_ref`; for lang-item trait bounds it calls `instantiate_lang_item_trait_ref`; for lifetime bounds it calls `ast_region_to_region`, `tcx`, and `push_region_bound` after wrapping the predicate with `bind_with_vars`.
Thin wrapper that computes all semantic bounds for a type parameter from its AST bounds. Calls `compute_bounds_inner`.

Filters AST bounds down to traits that may define a given associated type name, then computes semantic bounds from only that subset. Calls `tcx` and `trait_may_define_assoc_type` during filtering, then calls `compute_bounds_inner`.
Shared helper that initializes an empty `Bounds` set and fills it from AST bounds. Calls `add_bounds` with `ast_bounds.iter()` and an empty bound-variable list.

Turns an associated type or return-type notation binding from a trait bound into the corresponding semantic predicates, including resolving the defining trait through supertraits, checking visibility/stability, and tracking duplicate bindings. Calls `tcx`, `trait_defines_associated_item_named`, and `one_bound_for_assoc_type` to choose the target trait; then uses `adjust_ident_and_get_scope`, `associated_items`, `find_item_of_kind`, `check_stability`, and `emit_err`/`struct_span_err`-based diagnostics while constructing the final bound predicates.

Converts a resolved type path into a `Ty` by first calling `ast_path_args_for_ty` to build generic arguments, then either constructing a lazy type-alias `Ty::new_alias` when `def_kind`/`type_alias_is_lazy` indicate a lazy alias, or instantiating `tcx.at(span).type_of(did)` with those args.

Converts a `dyn`/trait-object bound list into the final object type by instantiating trait bounds, separating trait and projection predicates, expanding trait aliases, and validating the object-safe trait set. Calls `tcx`, repeatedly calls `instantiate_poly_trait_ref` to populate `Bounds`, then processes `predicates`, calls `expand_trait_aliases`, and uses `trait_is_auto` plus later object-type validation/diagnostic helpers such as `label_with_exp_info`.

Builds and emits the E0223 ambiguous-associated-type diagnostic, checking `tcx().resolutions(())` for the std-module confusion case and otherwise assembling context-sensitive suggestions with `span_suggestion_verbose` or `span_suggestions` before `emit()`.

Finds the unique trait bound on a type parameter that defines a named associated item by calling `get_type_parameter_bounds` to collect predicates and then delegating to `one_bound_for_assoc_type`, supplying candidates produced from `traits::transitive_bounds_that_define_assoc_item`.

Selects a single trait bound that defines the requested associated type or const by filtering candidates with `trait_defines_associated_item_named`; if none match it calls `complain_about_assoc_type_not_found`, and if multiple incompatible matches remain it emits ambiguity diagnostics using `tcx().associated_items(...).find_by_name_and_kind` and trait-path formatting before returning the chosen bound.

Resolves a type-relative path like `T::Assoc` by first probing ADTs with `probe_adt` to detect enum variants or inherent associated types, using `prohibit_generics` for invalid variant generics, then calling `lookup_inherent_assoc_ty` for inherent associated types or `one_bound_for_assoc_type` over trait/supertrait candidates to produce the final associated type, while also performing stability and diagnostic handling through `tcx` queries.
Looks up an associated type in a scope by calling `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked`, validating the result with `check_assoc_ty`, and returning the associated item `DefId` if found.

Converts a qualified path `<Self as Trait>::Assoc` into a projection type; when `Self` is omitted it gathers candidate implementing type names and calls `report_ambiguous_associated_type` to emit an error, otherwise it builds the trait ref with `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`, creates item args with `create_args_for_associated_item`, and returns `Ty::new_projection`.

Rejects generic arguments and associated type bindings on path segments that must not have them: it scans the segments’ args to classify forbidden lifetime/type/const/infer arguments, emits a tailored diagnostic through the supplied `extend` callback, and calls `prohibit_assoc_ty_binding` for associated type bindings.

Reconstructs which path segments in a value path carry generic arguments by analyzing the resolved `DefKind`, querying `tcx.generics_of`, and in ADT-related cases using `probe_adt`/parent relationships to produce a sequence of `PathSeg` entries describing the relevant definition and segment index.

Converts a resolved HIR path into a type by dispatching on `path.res`: it calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_args_for_ty` for opaque types, `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for ordinary nominal types, `def_ids_for_value_path_segments` plus `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for variant paths, `associated_path_to_ty` for type-relative paths, and `hir_id_to_bound_ty` for type parameters, while also emitting diagnostics for invalid resolutions.
Converts a HIR type into a semantic type by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with the default non-borrowed, non-path flags.
Converts a HIR type appearing inside a path by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with `in_path` enabled.

Core recursive HIR-type conversion routine. It converts slices, pointers, refs, tuples, bare fns, trait objects, paths, opaque defs, and type-relative paths by calling other helpers such as `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, `ty_of_fn`, `maybe_lint_bare_trait`, `conv_object_ty_poly_trait_ref`, `res_to_ty`, `impl_trait_ty_to_ty`, and `associated_path_to_ty`, then constructs the corresponding `Ty` node.

Builds the type for an `impl Trait`/opaque definition by iterating the item generics, resolving explicit lifetime arguments with `ast_region_to_region`, filling other parameters from `mk_param_from_def`, and then returning either `Ty::new_projection` for trait context or `Ty::new_opaque` otherwise.
Computes an argument type, reusing an expected type for `_` arguments by calling `record_ty`, and otherwise delegating to `ast_ty_to_ty`.

Constructs a function signature from HIR by collecting late-bound vars, walking generics for placeholder detection, converting inputs with `ty_of_arg`, converting the return type with `ast_ty_to_ty` when present, building the signature with `mk_fn_sig`/`bind_with_vars`, optionally calling `suggest_trait_fn_ty_for_impl_fn_infer` for `_` recovery, and finally validating region usage with `validate_late_bound_regions` after computing constrained and referenced late-bound regions.

When an impl method uses `_` in its signature, tries to recover the corresponding trait method type by computing the impl’s trait ref with `instantiate_mono_trait_ref` and `ast_ty_to_ty`, locating the associated method via `associated_items(...).find_by_name_and_kind`, instantiating its `fn_sig`, liberating late-bound regions, and returning the requested input or output type.

Checks that every referenced late-bound region is constrained by iterating `referenced_regions.difference(&constrained_regions)`, creating each diagnostic with `generate_err`, adding explanatory notes for anonymous lifetimes, and emitting the error.

Computes the lifetime bound for a trait object from its existential predicates when no explicit bound is given. It calls `tcx` to access the type context and `object_region_bounds` to derive candidate region bounds; if the derived set `is_empty`, it returns `None` so the caller can use the default. It then uses `iter`/`any` together with `is_static` to prefer `'static` when present, and otherwise checks whether all derived bounds are the same; if multiple distinct bounds exist, it calls `emit_err` to report an ambiguous lifetime bound before returning one of the derived regions.

When diagnosing a bare-trait object in an impl self type, suggests rewriting the impl as a blanket implementation if the implemented trait is local. Calls `tcx`, queries HIR with `hir`, `get_parent_item`, and `get_by_def_id`, checks the trait via `trait_def_id`, obtains source snippets through `source_map` and `span_to_snippet`, derives a parameter name with `next_type_param_name`, uses `span_for_param_suggestion`, and emits the edit with `multipart_suggestion`.

Detects trait-object syntax missing `dyn`, builds the appropriate insertion suggestion, and emits either a hard error or a lint depending on edition. Calls `tcx`, inspects source text via `source_map` and `span_to_prev_source`, emits suggestions with `multipart_suggestion_verbose`, and in the Edition 2021+ error path also calls `maybe_lint_blanket_trait_impl` before `emit`; otherwise it reports through `struct_span_lint_hir`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/expr.rs::i: Type-checks `expr` using `expected` as a hint by calling `check_expr_with_hint`, then enforces exact type equality between the inferred type and `expected` with `demand_eqtype`.

Checks an expression against a required type by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, permits the special `!`-to-any adjustment via `apply_adjustments`, and then enforces the final subtype relation with `demand_suptype_diag`, adding mismatch suggestions before emitting any error.

Checks `expr` against an `Expectation` by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, permits `!` expressions to adapt via `apply_adjustments` when needed, and finally validates that the resulting type is a subtype of the expected type with `demand_suptype_diag`. On mismatch it augments diagnostics with `emit_type_mismatch_suggestions`, invokes the provided `extend_err` callback, and emits the error.
Type-checks `expr` with `expected` as a hint by calling `check_expr_with_hint`, then requires the result to coerce to `expected` by calling `demand_coerce` without two-phase coercion.
A thin helper that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with `ExpectHasType(expected)` to type-check an expression using a concrete expected type as a hint.
Checks an expression by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, and if the usage requires a mutable place, calls `convert_place_derefs_to_mutable` to upgrade deref adjustments accordingly.
Default expression entry point that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with no expectation.
Checks an expression with place/mutability requirements by calling `check_expr_with_expectation_and_needs` with no type expectation.
Main convenience wrapper that forwards expression checking to `check_expr_with_expectation_and_args` with no call arguments or enclosing call expression.

Core expression-checking entry point that handles logging, unreachable-code and divergence bookkeeping, then dispatches path expressions to `check_expr_path` and all other expression forms to `check_expr_kind`, finally resolving the resulting type for recording and diagnostics.

Dispatches each HIR expression kind to its specialized checker, including `check_lit`, `check_binop`, `check_expr_assign`, `check_binop_assign`, `check_expr_unary`, `check_expr_addr_of`, `check_lang_item_path`, `check_expr_path`, `check_expr_asm`, `check_offset_of`, `check_expr_break`, `check_expr_return`, `check_expr_become`, `check_expr_let`, `check_expr_loop`, and `check_match`.

Checks a boxed expression by deriving an inner expectation from the outer boxed type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the boxed value, requiring that inner type to be sized with `require_type_is_sized`, and returning the corresponding boxed type via `mk_box`.

Checks a unary expression by first calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the operand, then resolving and validating the operator: deref uses `lookup_derefing`, while `!` and `-` use `check_user_unop` with builtin-type fast paths.

Checks `&`/`&raw` expressions by deriving an operand hint from the expected pointer/reference type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation_and_needs` on the operand, and then either calling `check_named_place_expr` for raw borrows or creating a fresh region for shared/mutable references.
Validates that a raw-borrow operand is a named place expression, allowing adjusted deref-based places, and emits an `AddressOfTemporaryTaken` error otherwise.
Resolves a lang item path by calling `resolve_lang_item_path` and returning the resolved type component.

Checks a value path by resolving it with `resolve_ty_and_res_fully_qualified_call`, diagnosing bad resolutions with `suggest_assoc_method_call` or variant-specific reporting, and otherwise instantiating it via `instantiate_value_path`; for function definitions it also records deferred intrinsic/transmute and sized-parameter checks.

Checks a `break` expression by consulting the enclosing breakable context, type-checking any break value with `check_expr_with_hint`, and coercing it into the loop’s break accumulator while producing targeted diagnostics for illegal or mismatched break values.

Checks a `return` expression by calling `emit_return_outside_of_fn_body` when outside a function body, otherwise either type-checking the returned value with `check_return_expr` or forcing unit into the return coercion; when outside a function but a value is present, it still calls `check_expr` on that value for error recovery.

Checks a return value inside a function by reading the expected return type from the return coercion, calling `check_expr_with_hint` on the returned expression, coercing it into the function return via the return coercion, and then calling `select_obligations_where_possible` to reroute opaque-type errors through `point_at_return_for_opaque_ty_error` when needed.
Rewrites fulfillment errors caused by `OpaqueReturnType(None)` so they point at the specific return expression span and type instead of a broader enclosing block span.

Validates that an assignment left-hand side is a syntactic place expression, and if not, produces a tailored diagnostic that may call `comes_from_while_condition` and `check_for_missing_semi` before applying caller-supplied error adjustments.
Walks parent HIR nodes to determine whether an expression originated from a `while` condition and, if so, invokes the provided callback on that condition expression.

Checks an `if`/`if-else` by calling `check_expr_has_type_or_error` on the condition, `warn_if_unreachable` for the then-branch, `check_expr_with_expectation` on each branch, and then coercing branch types together with branch-specific diagnostics and divergence tracking.

Checks assignment expressions by computing the expected unit-like result, issuing `=` vs `==` diagnostics when boolean context suggests it, type-checking operands via `check_expr`, `check_expr_with_needs`, and `check_expr_with_hint`, enforcing RHS-to-LHS coercion with `demand_coerce_diag`, and validating assignability with `check_lhs_assignable`.
Checks a `let` expression by calling `warn_if_unreachable` on its initializer and `check_decl` with statement-style rules, then returns `bool` unless recovery marked the expression as erroneous.

Checks loop expressions by creating an optional break-value coercion target from the expectation, running the body through `with_breakable_ctxt` and `check_block_no_value`, updating divergence based on whether breaks occur, and completing the accumulated break coercion when present.

Checks a method call by calling `check_expr` on the receiver, resolving its type, looking up the method with `lookup_method`, recording successful resolution with `write_method_call_and_enforce_effects` or diagnosing failure with `report_method_error`, and then calling `check_method_argument_types`.

Checks a cast by lowering the target type, calling `check_expr_with_expectation` on the source with `ExpectCastableToType`, resolving both sides, and either returning an immediate error or deferring the detailed validation through `cast::CastCheck::new`.

Checks array literals by choosing an element coercion target from the expectation or a fresh type variable, calling `check_expr_with_hint` for each element, coercing them through a `CoerceMany`, then calling `suggest_array_len` and returning the resulting array type.

Looks up the enclosing typed array context for an expression and, when it finds an inferred array-length placeholder, emits a diagnostic suggesting the concrete `array_len`. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks a const block in a fresh `FnCtxt`: it gathers locals, checks the body against the given expectation, enforces that the resulting type is sized, records the block type, and returns it. This method calls the listed method `check_expr_with_expectation`.

Type-checks an array repeat expression `[element; count]` by lowering/evaluating the length, optionally suggesting an explicit array length, deriving the element type from the expected array/slice type when possible, checking the element, enforcing repeat-copy requirements, building the array type, and registering a well-formedness obligation. This method calls the listed methods `suggest_array_len`, `check_expr_coercible_to_type`, `check_expr_has_type_or_error`, and `check_repeat_element_needs_copy_bound`.

Determines whether a repeat-expression element must satisfy `Copy`, exempting true constants and const blocks, classifying const-call/const-constructor cases for diagnostics, and requiring the `Copy` lang-item obligation only when the evaluated repeat count may exceed 1. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks a tuple expression by extracting expected field types from an expected tuple when available, coercing matching elements to those types, otherwise checking elements with no expectation, assembling the tuple type, propagating error types, and requiring the tuple initializer to be sized. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr_coercible_to_type` and `check_expr_with_expectation`.

Type-checks a struct literal by resolving the struct path, recovering by checking subexpressions on path-resolution failure, rejecting external non-exhaustive struct construction, checking all provided/base fields, and requiring the resulting ADT type to be sized. This method calls the listed methods `check_struct_path`, `check_struct_fields_on_error`, and `check_expr_struct_fields`.

Checks the fields of a struct literal against the chosen variant: it reconciles expectation-derived hints with the ADT type, tracks remaining and duplicate fields, resolves each supplied field, records field indices, validates stability and field types, reports unknown fields, checks field expressions with hints/coercions, registers well-formedness obligations, and emits diagnostics for missing fields or FRU-related mistakes. This method calls the listed methods `expected_inputs_for_expected_output`, `demand_eqtype`, `write_field_index`, `field_ty`, `report_unknown_field`, `check_expr_with_hint`, `demand_coerce_diag`, and `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.
Performs error-recovery checking for struct literal contents by still type-checking every explicit field expression and the optional base expression. This method calls the listed method `check_expr`.

Builds and emits the missing-fields diagnostic for a struct literal, formatting a readable list of omitted fields and, when there is at least one written field, delegating to a FRU typo suggestion path before emission. This method calls the listed method `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.

Detects when the last struct field expression is a half-open `Range` literal that likely should be functional record update syntax (`..expr`) instead of a field value, suppresses any previously stashed range type-mismatch diagnostic, extracts a short printable snippet for the range end, computes the span covering the mistaken `..` region, and attaches a `TypeMismatchFruTypo` subdiagnostic to the provided error. This method does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Reports that a struct literal cannot be constructed because of private fields, distinguishing explicitly used versus merely remaining private fields, labeling or noting them, and searching inherent impl items for constructor-like associated functions whose signatures match the ADT so it can suggest alternatives. It does not call other listed methods.

Emits the diagnostic for using an unknown field in a struct/variant literal, tailoring the message for enum variants vs other ADTs, suggesting tuple-style constructor syntax for tuple variants, and offering likely field-name corrections based on available visible fields. This method calls the listed methods `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.
Builds a list of accessible, stable field names for a variant while skipping already-used names, then returns the closest match to the requested field by calling `find_best_match_for_name`.

Collects suggestable field names from a variant, excluding fields already present in `skip_fields` and filtering through field-suggestability checks. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.
Formats a bounded, human-readable comma-separated series of field names, appending an `... and N others` suffix when the list is longer than the display limit. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks field access by checking and resolving the base expression, autodereferencing through candidate receiver types, locating direct or nested ADT fields, recording field indices, applying deref adjustments and obligations for accessible fields, handling tuple indexing syntax, and otherwise reporting private or nonexistent-field errors. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `find_adt_field`, `field_ty`, `write_field_index`, `ban_private_field_access`, and `ban_nonexisting_field`.

When the base type is an `impl Future`, checks whether the requested field exists on the future's `Output` type and, if so, suggests inserting `.await`; otherwise it just labels the field as unknown. It does not call other listed methods.

Builds and emits the main diagnostic for accessing a nonexistent field, specializing suggestions for arrays, raw pointers, type parameters, and opaque futures, then trying a method-call suggestion if calling the base expression would yield a type with the requested field, and adding the Rust-2018 `.await` note when relevant. This method calls the listed methods `no_such_field_err`, `maybe_suggest_array_indexing`, `suggest_first_deref_field`, `point_at_param_definition`, and `suggest_await_on_field_access`.

Emits the private-field-access diagnostic and, when appropriate, suggests calling an accessible method with the same name instead of reading the field. This method calls the listed method `private_field_err`.

Reports the error for treating a method as a field value, then suggests either removing wrapping parentheses for an accidental call pattern, adding call parentheses, or dereferencing first for raw-pointer-to-ADT cases where the field exists after dereference. It does not call other listed methods.

Augments a diagnostic for field access on a type parameter by locating the non-synthetic type parameter declaration in the current body and labeling where that parameter was introduced. It does not call other listed methods.

Produces diagnostics for an unknown field on a struct-like ADT: it first calls `suggest_field_name` to offer a similar field name, and if none is found, it labels the access and lists available fields using `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.

For mistaken tuple-style field syntax on arrays, labels the field as unknown and, when the field parses as an integer and the array length is evaluable, suggests rewriting `.n` as `[n]` with an applicability tuned by bounds confidence. It does not call other listed methods.
For raw-pointer field access, labels the field as unknown and suggests wrapping the base expression in an explicit dereference before accessing the field. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the base `no field` diagnostic and enriches it with suggestions for nested-field access paths, misspelled field names, and visible candidate field listings; it also unwraps `Option`/`Result`-like outer types when searching for nested matches. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy`, `check_for_nested_field_satisfying`, and `name_series_display`.

Autodereferences a base type and gathers visible, suggestable fields from non-enum ADTs, skipping wrappers whose fields are all private and capping the number of searched fields for compile-time cost. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.

Recursively searches through visible nested ADT fields up to depth three for a field satisfying the provided predicate, extending and returning the field path on success. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy` and `check_for_nested_field_satisfying` recursively.

Type-checks indexing expressions by checking both operands, resolving the base type, using normal indexing lookup when available, coercing the index to the required index type and retargeting obligation spans, otherwise probing for a nearly applicable `Index` impl with unsatisfied predicates, and finally emitting specialized diagnostics for non-indexable types such as tuples or pointers. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `lookup_indexing`, `point_at_index`, and `find_and_report_unsatisfied_index_impl`.
Scans fulfillment errors for `SliceIndex` trait obligations and, when found, rewrites their cause span to the provided span so indexing-related diagnostics point at the expression location.

Checks a `yield` expression against the current coroutine context. If coroutine types are available, it calls `check_expr_coercible_to_type` to coerce the yielded value to the coroutine's `yield_ty` and returns the coroutine `resume_ty`. Otherwise it emits an error through `dcx().emit_err`, calls `check_expr` on the yielded value to ensure it is still type-checked, and returns `unit`.

Checks one inline-assembly operand, using `check_expr_with_needs` to type-check the expression with either no place requirement for inputs or mutable-place requirement for outputs, then `require_type_is_sized` to enforce `Sized`. For non-inputs it rejects non-place expressions via `dcx().struct_span_err(...).emit()`. For inputs it calls `structurally_resolve_type` and, when the resolved type is a function item or reference, uses `demand_coerce` to coerce it respectively to a function pointer or raw pointer.

Checks an entire inline `asm!` expression and determines whether it yields `!` or `()`. It calls `check_expr_asm_operand` for each input/output operand, and for label operands it calls `check_block_with_expected` with unit expectation, then uses `demand_suptype` to require `()` when the label block does not diverge. It also restores divergence tracking for label blocks and returns `never` if the asm is guaranteed not to return, otherwise `unit`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/method/pro: Returns the underlying `FnCtxt` stored in `ProbeContext` via deref coercion; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Returns whether this receiver adjustment carries an unsizing step by pattern-matching on the enum variant; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Finds methods whose return type matches the requested type for diagnostics by first calling `probe_op` to collect candidate names through `ProbeContext::candidate_method_names`, then calling `probe_op` again for each name to resolve it with `ProbeContext::pick`, and finally returning the picked associated items.
Resolves a single method or associated item name for a receiver by calling `probe_op`, which runs `ProbeContext::pick` to perform candidate selection and return a `PickResult`.

Core probing driver that canonicalizes the receiver type, computes autoderef steps, builds a `ProbeContext` with `ProbeContext::new`, assembles candidates by calling `ProbeContext::assemble_inherent_candidates` and either `ProbeContext::assemble_extension_candidates_for_traits_in_scope` or `ProbeContext::assemble_extension_candidates_for_all_traits` depending on scope, and then executes the supplied probe operation.
Registers the query provider for method autoderef computation by wiring `providers.method_autoderef_steps` to `method_autoderef_steps`.

Computes the autoderef search steps for method probing, recording each reachable receiver form and possible final unsizing step for use by later probe logic; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs and initializes a fresh `ProbeContext` with empty candidate/diagnostic state; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Clears all accumulated candidates and diagnostic bookkeeping so the same probe context can be reused for a second search pass; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Adds a candidate to either the inherent or extension list after checking visibility in the current scope, or records the first inaccessible private candidate for diagnostics; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Walks all autoderef receiver steps and calls `assemble_probe` for each step’s receiver type to gather inherent candidates.

Dispatches inherent candidate assembly based on the probed receiver kind: it calls `assemble_inherent_candidates_from_object` for trait objects, `assemble_inherent_impl_candidates_for_type` for nominal types with inherent impls, `assemble_inherent_candidates_for_incoherent_ty` for incoherent primitive-like cases, and `assemble_inherent_candidates_from_param` for type parameters with trait bounds.
Finds inherent impls registered for an incoherent simplified type and calls `assemble_inherent_impl_probe` for each matching impl.
Loads all inherent impls for a nominal type and calls `assemble_inherent_impl_probe` on each impl to add applicable inherent method candidates.

Examines one inherent impl, skips duplicates, filters out items without a receiver while recording static candidates, computes transformed self/return types for receiver-bearing items, and then calls `push_candidate` to register each applicable inherent impl candidate.

Builds callable method candidates from a trait object by elaborating the principal trait and its supertraits with `elaborate_bounds`, computing adjusted receiver types for each item, and calling `push_candidate` to store the resulting object-based candidates.

Extracts trait bounds applicable to a type parameter, elaborates them with `elaborate_bounds`, filters out candidates whose transformed self type still needs inference, and calls `push_candidate` to add where-clause-derived method candidates.

Traverses transitive trait bounds and, for each trait item, either records static non-method items or invokes the supplied callback to build a candidate; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Collects extension candidates from traits visible at the lookup site, deduplicating trait IDs and calling `assemble_extension_candidates_for_trait` for each in-scope trait.
Collects extension candidates from every known trait for suggestion/diagnostic probing, deduplicating trait IDs and calling `assemble_extension_candidates_for_trait` for each trait.

Checks whether a method candidate’s function signature can accept the optional receiver type and produce the expected return type during probing; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Builds extension candidates for a trait: for trait aliases it calls `elaborate_bounds` to include supertrait items and then `push_candidate` for each generated candidate, while for ordinary non-auto traits it directly iterates trait items and records applicable method candidates.

Returns a deduplicated, sorted list of candidate method names from inherent and extension candidates, using `matches_return_type` to keep only candidates compatible with the requested return type when one is provided.

Performs final method selection by first calling `pick_core`; on failure it preserves diagnostic state, calls `reset`, expands the search with `assemble_extension_candidates_for_all_traits`, calls `pick_core` again to identify out-of-scope traits, and then returns a detailed error or fallback diagnostic result.
Runs the main selection pass by calling `pick_all_method`, and if stable-first picking is enabled and no result was found, calls `pick_all_method` again without unstable filtering.

Iterates over valid autoderef steps, instantiates each receiver type, and tries method lookup in order by calling `pick_by_value_method`, then `pick_autorefd_method` for shared and mutable references, and finally `pick_const_ptr_method`, returning the first successful pick.

Attempts method selection using the receiver type by value by calling `pick_method`; if successful, it adjusts the resulting pick’s autoderef count and may consult `AutorefOrPtrAdjustment::get_unsize` when folding an existing unsize adjustment into an inserted autoref for reference receivers.

Attempts method selection after adding an explicit shared or mutable reference to the receiver by constructing the referenced type, calling `pick_method`, and annotating the resulting pick with the corresponding autoref adjustment.

Attempts method selection by weakening a mutable raw pointer receiver to a const raw pointer, calling `pick_method` on that adjusted type, and marking the resulting pick with a `ToConstPtr` adjustment.

Searches inherent candidates first and then extension candidates, allowing unstable methods on the second pass, and returns the first successful pick. It explicitly calls `consider_candidates` for each candidate set and records accumulated unsatisfied predicates before returning `None` if no pick is found.

Resolves a method pick while optionally collecting unstable candidates; if the session is configured not to prefer stable methods first, it delegates directly to `pick_method_with_unstable`. Otherwise it explicitly calls `consider_candidates` over inherent and extension candidates, returns the first successful pick, and stores unsatisfied predicates only on the first collection pass.

Evaluates a slice of candidates for applicability, filters out `NoMatch` results, optionally collapses multiple matching trait candidates into one pick, removes unstable matches when collecting them, and then produces either an ambiguity error or a final pick. It explicitly calls `consider_probe` for each candidate, `collapse_candidates_to_trait_pick` when multiple candidates remain, `candidate_source` when building ambiguity data, and `Candidate::to_unadjusted_pick` for the final single-candidate result.
Returns whether two picks differ by comparing only their resolved `self_ty` and associated item `def_id`, ignoring other pick metadata. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Emits the unstable-name-collision lint when the chosen pick has competing unstable candidates, tailoring the help text to functions or trait constants and mentioning the relevant feature gate on nightly. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Builds a trait obligation for the given trait reference and asks trait selection to resolve it. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Classifies where a candidate came from for diagnostics, distinguishing inherent impls, trait/object/where-clause sources, and trait candidates that can be narrowed to a specific impl. For trait candidates it explicitly calls `select_trait_candidate` inside a probe to determine whether a unique user-defined impl should be reported instead of the trait itself.

Checks whether a single candidate can apply to the current receiver by relating self types, normalizing and instantiating relevant predicates, testing whether those obligations may hold, and performing trait selection when needed; it returns `Match`, `NoMatch`, or records potentially unsatisfied predicates for diagnostics. It explicitly calls `select_trait_candidate` when evaluating trait-based candidates.

If every applicable candidate comes from the same trait container, coalesces them into a single `TraitPick`; otherwise it leaves the ambiguity unresolved. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Searches for similarly named inherent methods for diagnostics by creating a fresh probe context, collecting candidate names, retrying each close name, and choosing the best Levenshtein-style match among applicable picks. It explicitly calls `assemble_inherent_candidates`, `candidate_method_names`, `reset`, and `pick_core` on the temporary probe context.

Determines whether an associated item is usable in the current lookup mode: method-call mode requires a `self` parameter, while path mode accepts functions and constants but rejects associated types. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Records a static candidate source for later diagnostics by appending it to the stored static-candidate list. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Computes the receiver type and optional return type used for probing: in method-call mode for functions it derives them from the transformed method signature, otherwise it falls back to the impl type with no return-type filter. It explicitly calls `xform_method_sig` for method-call function items.

Instantiates a method’s function signature for probing by substituting known parent generics, creating fresh inference variables for the method’s own generic parameters, and erasing late-bound regions from the result. It explicitly calls `erase_late_bound_regions` before returning the transformed signature.
Returns the bound self type of an impl together with fresh substitutions for that impl’s generics. It explicitly calls `fresh_item_substs` to create those substitutions.

Creates fresh substitutions for every generic parameter of an item, erasing lifetimes and introducing fresh type or const inference variables for type and const parameters. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Erases late-bound regions from a bound value using the type context and returns the resulting value. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Collects associated items from an impl or trait matching the current name policy: exact-name lookup, similar-name lookup for diagnostics, or all relevant items when no name is specified. It explicitly calls `is_relevant_kind_for_mode` to filter items in every lookup path.

Converts a resolved candidate into a `Pick` without autoderef or autoref adjustments, choosing the appropriate `PickKind` from the candidate kind and preserving any collected unstable alternatives. It does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Ambiguous`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Error(err)` to record a selection failure; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Adds a projection candidate when possible, deduplicates identical candidates, prefers `ParamEnv` candidates over others, and otherwise converts a conflicting single candidate into ambiguity. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Handles higher-ranked projection equality by instantiating the obligation binder with placeholders inside a probe and then calling `project_and_unify_type`. It converts mismatches into `MismatchedProjectionTypes` and, when experimenting with extended GATs, filters out obligations that mention the newly created universe before returning `Holds`.

Solves a concrete projection equality by first calling `opt_normalize_projection_type` to normalize the projection, then replacing opaque types in the expected term with inference variables, and finally equating the normalized and expected terms. It returns `Holds` with accumulated obligations on success, or reports failed normalization, recursion, or mismatched projection types.
Creates an empty obligation list, calls `normalize_to` to normalize the given foldable value, and returns both the normalized value and the collected obligations packaged in `Normalized`.
Delegates normalization to `normalize_with_depth_to` with recursion depth 0, forwarding the caller-provided obligation sink.

Convenience entry point for normalization at a given recursion depth: it allocates an obligation buffer, calls `normalize_with_depth_to`, and packages the normalized value together with the collected obligations.

Normalizes a foldable value into a caller-provided obligation buffer by constructing an `AssocTypeNormalizer` with `AssocTypeNormalizer::new` and then calling its `fold` method under stack protection.

Like `normalize_with_depth_to`, but uses a normalizer configured to avoid eager inference replacement: it calls `AssocTypeNormalizer::new_without_eager_inference_replacement` and then invokes `AssocTypeNormalizer::fold` under stack protection.

Checks whether a value contains projection-, inherent-, const-projection-, or optionally opaque-related type flags that require normalization, depending on the `Reveal` mode. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured for normal eager inference replacement, after asserting the old trait solver path is in use. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured to avoid eager inference replacement. It does not call other methods in this list.

Top-level normalization helper for the normalizer: it resolves inference variables, asserts there are no escaping bound vars, calls `needs_normalization` to fast-path already-normal values, and otherwise recursively folds the value.
Returns the type context for the normalizer by calling `self.selcx.tcx()`.
Enters a new binder universe, calls `super_fold_with` to recursively normalize the binder contents, then exits the universe.

Core type-normalization folder for associated types and opaque types. It first skips work when `needs_normalization` is false, otherwise recursively folds substructure with `super_fold_with`, checks recursion limits via `tcx`, and normalizes projection types by calling `normalize_projection_type` or `opt_normalize_projection_type`; it also uses bound-variable replacement and placeholder restoration around projection normalization when binders are involved.
Normalizes constants unless lazy normalization is enabled. It calls `super_fold_with` to fold nested structure, then evaluates the folded constant with `with_replaced_escaping_bound_vars` and `eval`.
Normalizes a predicate only when `allow_normalization` and `needs_normalization` both permit it; in that case it calls `super_fold_with`, otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged.

Utility that temporarily replaces escaping bound vars with placeholders before running a closure, then restores them afterward. When escaping vars are present it calls `BoundVarReplacer::replace_bound_vars`, runs the callback, and then calls `PlaceholderReplacer::replace_placeholders`; otherwise it just runs the callback directly.

Entry point for converting bound regions, types, and consts into placeholders while recording reverse mappings. It constructs a `BoundVarReplacer`, folds the input through it, and returns the rewritten value plus the collected maps.
Finds or lazily creates the universe index associated with a given de Bruijn level, extending the tracked universe stack as necessary. It does not call other methods in this list.
Returns the inference context's type context directly.
Adjusts the current Debruijn depth for a nested binder, calls `super_fold_with` to replace bound variables inside it, then restores the previous depth.

Replaces late-bound regions at or above the current binder with placeholder regions, using `universe_for` to choose the universe and `mk_region` to build the replacement; regions outside that range are left unchanged.

Replaces bound types at or above the current binder with placeholder types, calling `universe_for` and `mk_ty` for the replacement; if the type merely contains deeper bound variables, it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse, otherwise it returns the type unchanged.
Replaces bound constants at or above the current binder with placeholder constants, using `universe_for` and `mk_const`; for all other constants it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse.
Calls `super_fold_with` only when the predicate contains variables bound at or above the current binder depth; otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged.
Entry point for converting placeholders back into bound vars using previously recorded maps and universe information. It constructs a `PlaceholderReplacer` and folds the input through it.
Returns the inference context's type context directly.
Skips binders with no placeholders or infer regions; otherwise adjusts binder depth, calls `super_fold_with` to restore placeholders under the binder, and then restores the previous depth.

Resolves inference regions opportunistically, then converts mapped placeholder regions back into late-bound regions by consulting the stored universe mapping and calling `tcx().mk_region`; unmapped regions are returned as-is.

Converts mapped placeholder types back into bound types using the stored universe mapping and `tcx().mk_ty`; if the type still contains placeholders or infer regions in substructure, it calls `super_fold_with`, otherwise it returns the type unchanged.
Converts mapped placeholder constants back into bound constants via `tcx().mk_const`; for non-placeholder constants it calls `super_fold_with` to recurse.

Public entry point that normalizes an associated-type projection to a `Term`. It explicitly calls `opt_normalize_projection_type`; if that returns no concrete result due to ambiguity, it falls back to `infer_projection` to create an inference variable and deferred obligations.

Attempts to normalize a projection type with recursion detection and projection-cache support, returning either a concrete normalized term, ambiguity, or in-progress recursion. It explicitly calls `project` to compute the projection when cache lookup does not decide the result, and then records progress, ambiguity, or errors back into the cache while extending the caller's obligations.

Produces an error-tolerant normalized term by creating a fresh type or const inference variable and adding the projected trait obligation so trait solving can continue. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Constructs a `Progress` value whose term is an error type and whose obligations list is empty; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Appends additional obligations to an existing `Progress` result and returns it; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Top-level projection solver that checks recursion and prior errors, assembles candidates from the parameter environment, trait definition, object bounds, and impl selection, then either confirms a unique candidate or returns ambiguity/error/no-progress. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_param_env`, `assemble_candidates_from_trait_def`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `confirm_candidate`, `Progress::error`, and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`/`ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error` indirectly through candidate assembly outcomes.

Builds a projection candidate for an impl-trait-in-trait associated item by deriving the parent trait predicate and attempting selection with `select` inside `commit_if_ok`. On success it records `ProjectionCandidate::ImplTraitInTrait` via `push_candidate`; on uncertainty it calls `mark_ambiguous`, and on selection failure it calls `mark_error`.
Collects projection candidates from the caller bounds in the parameter environment. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Scans item bounds from the trait definition for matching projection clauses, pushes matching trait-definition candidates, and marks ambiguity when matching cannot be decided. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Builds projection candidates from object type projection bounds when the trait supports object-based projection, and marks ambiguity if the self type is still a type variable. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Filters a stream of projection predicates by associated item and argument compatibility, probes whether each can match the goal, and either pushes a candidate or marks ambiguity. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Selects the underlying trait obligation to derive impl-based projection candidates, then records ambiguity, selection error, or a usable builtin/user-defined candidate while accounting for specialization and builtin trait cases. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error`.

Turns a chosen projection candidate into concrete projected progress by delegating to the appropriate confirmation routine and then opportunistically resolving inferred regions in the resulting term. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` for `ParamEnv`, `Object`, and `TraitDef` candidates, and `confirm_select_candidate` for `Select` candidates.

Confirms an impl-selected candidate by dispatching to the appropriate builtin or user-defined confirmation path based on the selected impl source and trait kind. It calls `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_fn_kind_helper_candidate`, and `confirm_builtin_candidate`.

Handles projection for generator associated types (`Yield`/`Return`) by resolving the obligation self type as a generator, normalizing its generator signature with `normalize_with_depth`, building the corresponding generator projection predicate via `generator_trait_ref_and_outputs`, and then delegating final confirmation to `confirm_param_env_candidate`. It returns that result augmented with the incoming nested obligations and the obligations produced during signature normalization via `with_addl_obligations`.

Confirms a `DiscriminantKind`-style projection by resolving the self type, constructing the corresponding discriminant projection predicate, and delegating final confirmation to `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Confirms a `Pointee`/metadata projection by computing pointer metadata for the resolved self type, normalizing nested metadata types with `normalize_with_depth_to`, optionally adding a `Sized` obligation, and then delegating to `confirm_param_env_candidate`; it returns the result augmented with the extra obligations via `with_addl_obligations`.
Normalizes a function pointer signature and confirms its callable output projection via the shared callable path. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Builds the effective callable signature for closures or coroutine-closures, including async/coroutine-specific output construction when needed, then confirms the resulting callable projection. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Constructs the `FnOnce::Output` projection predicate from a callable signature and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Confirms a projection candidate taken from the parameter environment by instantiating the cached binder, normalizing the obligation projection and optionally the candidate projection with `normalize_with_depth_to`, equating the two projections via inference, and on success extending obligations and calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations`; on failure it returns an error term.

Confirms a projection candidate coming from a selected impl by locating the associated item in the impl, rebasing and translating trait/impl arguments, building the resulting associated term from the impl item definition, checking argument compatibility, and then calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations` before instantiating the term; if the impl item is missing or incompatible it returns an error progress.

Checks whether the substitution list matches the associated item's generic parameter structure and argument kinds. It calls `generics_of` to fetch the associated item's generics, `as_slice` to view the substitutions as generic arguments, and then delegates the recursive validation to `check_substs_compatible_inner`.

Recursively validates that a generic argument slice is structurally compatible with a `Generics` definition: it compares `count` against `len`, uses `split_at` to separate parent and local arguments, calls `generics_of` to load parent generics, recursively calls `check_substs_compatible_inner` for the parent chain, and then uses `zip` plus `unpack` to ensure each local argument kind matches its corresponding type, lifetime, or const parameter.

Confirms an impl-trait-in-trait projection by finding the concrete associated definition with `assoc_def`, normalizing the impl method predicates with `normalize_with_depth_to`, converting them into nested obligations, and normalizing the bound impl-trait result type with `normalize_to` before returning the final projected term and obligations.

Collects and adds the associated item's own declared predicates as nested obligations by instantiating the item's predicates, normalizing each predicate with `normalize_with_depth_to`, choosing an appropriate obligation cause, and pushing each normalized predicate as a deeper obligation.

Finds the concrete associated item definition for an impl, first checking the impl's own item map directly and otherwise querying specialization ancestors with `leaf_def`; it returns the matching `LeafDef` or reports an internal bug if no associated item exists.
Trait method contract for deriving a projection-cache key from a poly projection predicate and selection context.

Builds a `ProjectionCacheKey` for a poly projection predicate only when it has no bound vars. It explicitly calls `ProjectionCacheKey::new` after resolving inference variables in the predicate's projection type with `resolve_vars_if_possible`.
Adds the intercrate ambiguity explanation to a diagnostic by calling `intercrate_ambiguity_hint` to build the message and `note` to attach it.
Builds and returns a human-readable ambiguity hint string for each `IntercrateAmbiguityCause` variant, using `String::new` for missing self types and `clone` for reservation-impl messages.

Constructs a fresh `SelectionContext` with standard query mode, recursive inductive-cycle handling, no intercrate ambiguity tracking, and initializes the freshener by calling `freshener` on the inference context.
Constructs a `SelectionContext` configured for intercrate trait selection by reusing `SelectionContext::new` and overriding the `intercrate` flag to `true`. Calls `SelectionContext::new`.
Constructs a `SelectionContext` with an explicit `TraitQueryMode` by calling `SelectionContext::new` and overriding the `query_mode` field.
Enables collection of intercrate ambiguity causes after asserting intercrate mode with `is_intercrate`, ensuring tracking is not already active, and initializing the set with `default`.
Drains and returns the collected intercrate ambiguity causes after asserting intercrate mode with `is_intercrate`, using `take` and `unwrap_or_default`.
Returns the underlying `InferCtxt` reference stored in this selection context; it does not invoke any other methods from the provided Methods List.
Returns the underlying `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context.
Reports whether this selection context is running in intercrate mode by reading the inference context flag.
Wraps a monomorphic `TraitObligation` into a `PolyTraitObligation` by cloning the cause and using `ty::Binder::dummy`, then calls `poly_select`.

Starts candidate selection for a root obligation by creating a fresh provisional evaluation cache, building the initial stack with `push_stack` over `TraitObligationStackList::empty`, and then calling `candidate_from_obligation`.

Checks whether a predicate obligation may hold in standard query mode by calling `evaluate_root_obligation`, then unwrapping the result with `expect` and converting the evaluation to a boolean with `may_apply`.

Evaluates a root predicate obligation in a probe by calling `evaluation_probe`, normalizing the goal with `resolve_vars_if_possible`, recursively evaluating it via `evaluate_predicate_recursively` on an empty stack, and downgrading the result with `shallow_resolve` and `max` if inference variables changed.

Runs an evaluation closure inside an inference probe by calling `probe`, executing `op`, then checking soundness and side effects with `universe`, `leak_check`, `opaque_types_added_in_snapshot`, and `region_constraints_added_in_snapshot`, using `max` to weaken the result when needed.

Evaluates a sequence of nested obligations by setting each obligation depth from the parent with `set_depth_from_parent`, calling `evaluate_predicate_recursively` for each one, and combining results with `max` while fast-returning on `EvaluatedToErr`.

Recursively evaluates a general predicate obligation. It calls `check_recursion_limit` using the current stack head when present, then dispatches by predicate kind inside `ensure_sufficient_stack`: trait predicates are forwarded to `evaluate_trait_predicate_recursively`; subtype and coerce predicates use `subtype_predicate` or `coerce_predicate` and then `evaluate_predicates_recursively`; well-formedness, projection, const-evaluatable, and outlives-related cases evaluate through the corresponding inference or obligation-producing paths; cycle-related paths use `coinductive_match`, `update_reached_depth`, and recursive calls to `evaluate_predicate_recursively`/`evaluate_predicates_recursively` to combine nested results.

Recursively evaluates a trait predicate with caching and cycle handling. It may canonicalize the param-env for better caching, then calls `push_stack`, checks cached results with `check_evaluation_cache` and provisional results with `get_provisional`, detects recursion with `check_evaluation_cycle`, computes a fresh result by calling `in_task` around `evaluate_stack`, may re-normalize and re-evaluate via `try_normalize_with_depth_to`, `evaluate_predicate_recursively`, or recursive `evaluate_trait_predicate_recursively`, and finally stores results with `insert_evaluation_cache` or provisional-cache insertion as appropriate.

Detects whether the current trait obligation forms a cycle with an earlier stack frame by scanning the stack, marking the cycle depth with `update_reached_depth`, building the participating predicate sequence using `tcx` and `to_predicate`, and then calling `coinductive_match`; coinductive cycles evaluate to success, while inductive cycles are converted with `into` from the current cycle policy.

Evaluates a trait-obligation stack frame while guarding against recursive unbound-input loops. It checks for repeated fresh trait references with `match_fresh_trait_refs`, returns ambiguity for that conservative recursion case, otherwise calls `candidate_from_obligation` and then `evaluate_candidate` on the selected candidate.
Returns whether every predicate in a detected cycle is coinductive by calling `is_coinductive` on each predicate with `tcx`.
Determines whether a predicate is coinductive for recursion handling: trait clauses are checked via `tcx`, and well-formed predicates are treated as coinductive; otherwise returns false. Calls `tcx`.

Evaluates a specific selection candidate by calling `evaluation_probe`, cloning the candidate, confirming it with `confirm_candidate`, recursively evaluating its nested obligations via `evaluate_predicates_recursively`, and then weakening the result with `max` if the freshened trait predicate has erased regions.

Looks up a trait-evaluation result in the caches, first refusing to cache in intercrate mode via `is_intercrate`, then using `tcx`, `can_use_global_caches`, and `get` to query the global cache before falling back to the local inference-context cache.

Stores a completed evaluation result unless it is stack-dependent or intercrate-specific. It checks `is_stack_dependent`, `is_intercrate`, and `can_use_global_caches`; if globally cacheable and inference-free it inserts through `tcx().evaluation_cache.insert`, otherwise it inserts into the local evaluation cache.
Raises the recursion depth of each obligation in the iterator by iterating with `for_each` and setting each depth to one more than the `max` of the current depth and the provided minimum.

Enforces the trait-selection recursion limit by consulting `recursion_limit` and `value_within_limit`; on overflow it either returns a canonical overflow, converts existing taint via `tainted_by_errors`, or reports the overflow using `err_ctxt().report_overflow_obligation`.
Checks the recursion limit for an obligation by delegating directly to `check_recursion_depth` with the obligation's `recursion_depth`.

Executes a selection operation inside an anonymous dep-graph task by calling `tcx().dep_graph.with_anon_task`, then marks the resulting dependency with `read_index` and returns both the result and dep-node index.

Filters a candidate list to keep only impl candidates whose polarity matches the obligation or is reservation-only, using `tcx` to query `impl_polarity`, while passing through non-impl candidates unchanged.

Filters out reservation impl candidates by treating an `ImplCandidate` with reservation polarity as ambiguous; it calls `tcx` to query impl polarity and reservation attributes, records an `IntercrateAmbiguityCause::ReservationImpl` when tracking is enabled, and otherwise returns the original candidate.

Checks whether the current trait obligation is knowable in intercrate mode. It calls `is_intercrate` to fast-path non-intercrate cases, uses `resolve_vars_if_possible` to simplify the predicate, calls `tcx`, and then delegates to `coherence::trait_ref_is_knowable` on the obligation's trait ref.
Determines whether selection may use the global cache: it returns false if the parameter environment has inference variables or if `is_intercrate` is true, and true otherwise.

Looks up a previously computed candidate result in the selection caches. It calls `is_intercrate` to disable caching in intercrate mode, `tcx` and `skip_binder` to form the cache key, then calls `can_use_global_caches` and checks the global cache before falling back to the local inference-context cache.

Determines whether a selection result is safe to cache. It calls `is_intercrate` to reject all intercrate caching, and for `ParamCandidate` results only allows caching when the trait ref has no inference variables.

Stores a candidate result in either the global or local selection cache. It calls `tcx`, `skip_binder`, `can_cache_candidate`, and `can_use_global_caches`; cacheable, inference-free, non-canonical-overflow results go to `tcx.selection_cache`, otherwise they are inserted into the local `infcx.selection_cache`.

Finds definition-bound trait clauses on a projection or opaque self type that can satisfy the given obligation. It calls `resolve_vars_if_possible`, `instantiate_binder_with_placeholders`, and then, for each bound from `item_bounds`, probes by calling `match_normalize_trait_ref`; matching bounds are deduplicated after normalization and their indices are returned.

Normalizes a candidate trait bound and checks whether it can be matched against a placeholder obligation trait ref. It first compares trait `def_id`s, then calls `project::normalize_with_depth` under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, and finally uses `infcx.at(...).sup(...)` to test the match, returning the normalized trait ref only if no inference variables or placeholders remain.

Evaluates whether a where-clause trait ref may satisfy the current stack obligation inside an evaluation probe. It calls `evaluation_probe`, then `match_where_clause_trait_ref`, and on success calls `evaluate_predicates_recursively` with `stack.list()` and the produced obligations.

Tests whether an environment projection predicate can match a projection obligation, optionally normalizing the candidate projection first. It calls `instantiate_binder_with_fresh_vars`, optionally `project::normalize_with_depth_to` via `ensure_sufficient_stack`, then uses `infcx.at(...).sup(...)` and `evaluate_predicates_recursively` to validate nested obligations; on success it calls `tcx` and checks GAT argument inference to distinguish `Yes` from `Ambiguous`.

Compares two evaluated selection candidates and decides whether the `victim` should be discarded in favor of `other`, using priority rules, specialization, region-sensitive matching, and overlap checks. Lowers a resolved AST path into an HIR `Path` starting from a `NodeId`. It first obtains the full resolution with `expect_full_res`, converts that resolution with `lower_res`, and then delegates the actual path construction to `lower_path_extra`.

Lowers one AST `PathSegment` into an HIR path segment by converting its identifier, resolution, and generic arguments, while diagnosing invalid parenthesized generics, return-type notation misuse, and missing angle brackets. Lowers angle-bracketed generic arguments and associated-item constraints into an intermediate `GenericArgsCtor`, while also reporting whether the arguments are effectively elidable in optional-parameter mode. Lowers parenthesized function-trait-style generic arguments by turning inputs into a tuple argument and the return type into an `Output` associated type constraint, while enforcing the allowed `impl Trait` contexts and propagating async-bound feature tagging. The observed bug domain is trait-associated const resolution on a type-relative path in a generic context, especially impl matching/projection for `impl<T> Trait for &'static T`, which belongs much more to name resolution, type checking, or trait solving than to per-segment HIR lowering. While this method does attach resolution info to segments, nothing in its shown logic suggests a lifetime- or associated-const-specific semantic decision that would explain erroneous acceptance/rejection of this case. So it is only a very weak candidate fix location.
